chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abi Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

He said: Indeed, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, did not create anything except that He intended it to be worshipped, and He did not create anything except that He intended it to be a means of drawing near to Him, and He did not create anything except that He intended its knowledge to be learned, and He did not create anything except that He intended it to be a source of blessing.

So He gave precedence to Salat above all other things, because it is the first thing for which the servant will be called to account. If it is accepted, what is beside it is accepted; and if it is rejected, what is beside it is rejected.
And Zakat was given precedence over all other wealth, because it purifies the wealth and makes it grow.
And Hajj was given precedence over all other deeds, because it is the Pillar of Allah on His earth.
And Sawm (fasting) was given precedence over all other deeds, because it is a shield from the Fire.
And Jihad was given precedence over all other deeds, because it is a gate from the gates of Paradise.
I asked: How is one called to account for it? He said: One will be called to account for it on the Day of Resurrection.
ai.seo_question: Why is Salat considered the first deed to be judged in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidating the teleological purpose of creation, where all entities are destined for worship, nearness, knowledge, or blessing. This narration underscores the foundational role of the five pillars—Salat, Zakat, Hajj, Sawm, and Jihad—as the primary mechanisms for achieving divine acceptance, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the interconnection between ritual practice and spiritual intent (niyyah).
